task: Primary-source followup: alliance defense overshoot and Company Fraud capped payout
scope: Source-only; no summary/questions/keys/readers consulted. No unverified FAQ used as ruling evidence.

defense.question: Does a newly exhausted strength-2 local alliance successfully defend attack strength 1, despite exact-equality wording?
defense.conclusion: No verified primary clarification resolving this exact overshoot case was located. Do not represent either >= or exact-equality interpretation as a found designer ruling.

primary_evidence.heading: Local Alliances
primary_evidence.text: Local alliances are temporary Army pieces. Their strength can be used for two purposes: the Deploy action and to defend against threats in India during the Events in India phase. Each piece can only be used once on the turn they are purchased, and its strength cannot be split among more than one purpose.

primary_evidence.heading: Mounting Defense
primary_evidence.text: The Commander associated with the region must exhaust pieces in the Army equal to the strength of the Crisis or as many as possible. If the newly-exhausted pieces do not equal the strength of the Crisis, the Crisis succeeds. Perform the steps of Region Loss (page 29).

primary_evidence.heading: Events in India
primary_evidence.text: If the Crown is a Commander and must defend a Crisis, you choose which pieces will be exhausted to meet the Crisis. [2P ONLY] The player holding the Player Button chooses.
primary_evidence.limitation: Does not resolve an alliance overshooting strength requirement.

additional_current_site_check.description: Publisher-branded Rules Library, displayed 4th Printing (Work in Progress). Its embedded Mounting Defense text preserves the same exact-equality wording; no overshoot clarification found.
additional_current_site_check.exact_embedded_text:
The Commander associated with the region must exhaust pieces in the Army equal to the strength of the Crisis or as many as possible. If the newly-exhausted pieces do not equal the strength of the Crisis, the Crisis succeeds. Perform the steps of Region Loss.

If the attack failed, remove all unrest in the attacked region and the Commander associated with the region should take a trophy token.

company_fraud.question: Is payout capped to the actual reduction in Company Balance when twice highest roll exceeds current Balance?
company_fraud.answer: Yes. Reduce Balance no lower than zero; take only the actual amount removed. Example: highest roll 6, Balance £10 -> Balance £0 and player takes £10, not £12.

primary_evidence.exact_case_and_option2_excerpt: (For example, a 6 is rolled (doubled to 12), but the current Company Balance is 10 pounds.) ... 2. The Company Balance is reduced to zero and the player takes 10 pounds from the Bank.
primary_evidence.exact_full_body:
The text of Company Fraud Blackmail card is:
[q]Play anytime on a turn before Company expenses are paid.  Roll one die for each of your officeholders.  Lower the Company Balance equal to twice highest roll and take that much from the bank.[/q]

As the card doesn't say, 'Play immediately before Company expenses are paid', I assume that it can be paid before the Revenue Phase for the turn, at a time when the holder might need some extra cash.  What is the position if the die roll would result in the Company Balance being lowered by an amount that exceeds the current Company Balance?  (For example, a 6 is rolled (doubled to 12), but the current Company Balance is 10 pounds.) The track doesn't contain 'negative spaces.'

I can envisage 3 possible possibilities.
1.  The Company Balance is reduced to zero and the player takes 12 pounds from the Bank.
2. The Company Balance is reduced to zero and the player takes 10 pounds from the Bank.
3. The *[-]Company[/-] [I]Player[/I] takes 12 pounds from the Bank and the Company Balance is notionally reduced to -2 pounds, meaning that the Chairman needs to take debt in the Company Operation Phase (if the card were played before that phase) or the Company needs to take an Emergency Loan (if the card were played in the period between the Chairman acting in the Company Operating Phase and the payment of company expenses in the  Revenue Phase).

Reading the card literally and noting there is no negative space of the Company Balance Track, I'd guess that the answer would be #1.  But I'm not sure and might very well be overlooking something.

* Edit: I found a really bad error in #3.  Now fixed.

primary_evidence.author: Cole Wehrle
primary_evidence.exact_full_body: #2 is correct. I'll see about clarifying the card.

modern_card_consistency.text: Play at the start of the Revenue phase. Roll one die for each of your officeholders. Lower the Company Balance equal to twice the highest roll (to a minimum of zero) and take that much from the bank.
modern_card_consistency.note: Designer ruling resolves the referent of that much; modern errata changes timing/floor but does not contradict the capped-payout ruling.
